newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Persetel drops further after German buy.
newsitem.headline: Persetel drops further after German buy.

text.p: Shares in South African information technology group Persetel Holdings Ltd shed eight percent of their value in morning trade on Tuesday following the group's announcement of a major German buy.
On Monday the firm announced it would buy a controlling stake in German firm Telemation AG, but said it would not reveal its purchse price.

Dealers and analysts said the drop was largely due to the dilutive effect of Persetel's plans to fund the acquisition by issuing 70 million new shares -- a massive dilution of its existing 186 million share capital.
"A large part of this drop is the dilution," one analyst said.
By 0913 GMT the firm's stock was down 310 cents to 34.40 rand, following a drop of four percent on Monday.

Persetel shares have been a star performer on the Joahnnesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) recently and rocketed almost 400 percent since the beginning of last year on the back of an 80 percent surge in attributable income in the year to end May, 1996, and the acquisition of numerous data businesses last year.

Dealers said there were worries over the price of the German purchase that were also now hitting the stock. They said many analysts had worked out differing values and there was confusion as to whether the buy had been expensive.
"Some analysts have one price and they say its overpaid, and some have other prices that say its in-line," one market source said.
Persetel said it would stick to its strategy of expanding by acquisition in the sector, which was one of the top-performing on the JSE in 1996.
"We have said before that we will be looking at one or two other acquisitions before the end of the year," chairman Roux Marnitz told Reuters on Monday.
